title: San Francisco against what research says such programmes achieve
question: For each kind of programme the City funds, what result does the research literature say to expect, and is there a San Francisco figure to set beside it?
finding: Of 30 published benchmarks for supportive housing, rapid rehousing, shelter, treatment, workforce, violence interruption, after-school and meal programmes, a San Francisco figure of the same kind could be found on disk for 6. Home-delivered meals: benchmark $11.06 total (incl. volunteer and donated value); San Francisco $9.44 of City money per meal in fiscal year 2025 (home-delivered and centre meals together; providers add federal, State and donated money on top). Permanent supportive housing / Housing First: benchmark $16,479 median (middle half $13,120 to $26,452); San Francisco $17,000 per unit vs $13,748 for Bay Area tax-credit projects (building operating cost only, services not included). Permanent supportive housing / Housing First: benchmark 86% housed (vs 36% usual care); San Francisco 97% of people in permanent housing stayed or left for other permanent housing (federal fiscal year 2024). For the other 24, including treatment completion and every violence-interruption and after-school measure, nothing published lets San Francisco be compared.
how: The benchmarks were transcribed by the download step from federal evaluations, systematic reviews and randomized trials, each with its design and page. Beside each one this screen puts the nearest San Francisco figure already computed in this file or recorded in a saved evaluation, and says who recorded it. Where the San Francisco figure measures something different it is left out rather than forced.
limits: No pair here is a like-for-like test. Research figures come from particular places, years and populations (the largest rapid-rehousing study covers families, not single adults), dollar figures are in each study's own year, and several San Francisco figures are the department's own. A benchmark met does not show the programme caused the result; only a study with a comparison group can, and almost no San Francisco programme has one.
